claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is/are the child/children you're claiming for?**

To help determine eligibility, I need to know:
- How many children do you have?
- What age is each child?

The rules are different depending on whether the child is:
- **Under 16 years old** (generally eligible)
- **16-19 years old** (may be eligible if in full-time education or training)
- **20 or over** (not eligible)

Please tell me about each child you're considering claiming for.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son, Alex. He's 7 years old, so still quite young.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information! That's great – Alex is 7 years old, so he's in the under-16 category, which means he should generally qualify. Let me continue with the eligibility checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is 7 years old, I expect the answer is no – he's not working. Please confirm this for me.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, he's not working at all. He's only 7, so he's just at primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me continue with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

In other words, is he not claiming any state benefits directly for himself?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name. He's just a young child, so nothing like that applies to him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Given that he's 7 years old and at primary school, I assume the answer is no – he's not in any apprenticeship. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not. He's far too young for an apprenticeship - he's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. **Do you normally live in the UK?**

There are several ways you might meet the residency requirements:

1. **You normally live in the UK** – This is the most straightforward path
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status and are working** (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3+ months)
4. **You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work**
5. **You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources** (and not claiming certain benefits)
6. **You have pre-settled status and studying** (with sufficient resources)
7. **You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national**
8. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** (in certain qualifying countries)

Which of these applies to your situation? Or do you simply live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad, not as a Crown servant or anything like that - we've just moved overseas.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. So you're living abroad but not as a Crown servant. Let me check a few more details to see if you might still qualify under the residency rules.

**Do you have any of the following immigration statuses?**

1. **Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (EUSS)
2. **Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (EUSS)

Or are you a UK/Irish citizen living abroad without any of these statuses?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have settled or pre-settled status. I'm just living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Based on what you've told me, it appears you don't meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit. The rules require that you normally live in the UK, or meet one of the special circumstances (such as having settled/pre-settled status, being a Crown servant abroad, or being in certain other qualifying situations).

Since you're living abroad without meeting any of these special circumstances, unfortunately **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex because you do not meet the residency requirements.

**Reason:** Child Benefit requires that you normally live in the UK, or meet one of the special circumstances. Since you're living abroad without settled status, pre-settled status, or another qualifying circumstance, you don't meet these requirements.

**What you might do:**

- If your situation changes and you move back to the UK, you would likely become eligible at that point
- If you obtain settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, you may qualify under different criteria
- For more information, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. If you have any other questions or if your circumstances change, feel free to ask.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but thank you for explaining it clearly. I understand now that living abroad means I can't claim it. I appreciate your help in going through everything with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you, even though it's not the outcome you were hoping for. 

It's completely understandable to be disappointed, but I'm pleased the explanation was clear. If your circumstances change in the future – such as if you move back to the UK or your immigration status changes – please feel free to come back and we can reassess your eligibility at that time.

Thank you for using this service, and I wish you all the best with Alex and your family abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you so much for your kind words and help. Take care!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're very welcome! Take care as well, and all the best to you and Alex! 😊

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you! Goodbye!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Goodbye! 👋
